newsitem.title: USA: Majority believe Perot should debate - poll.
newsitem.headline: Majority believe Perot should debate - poll.

text.p: A majority of Americans want Reform Party candidate Ross Perot included in debates with President Bill Clinton and Republican challenger Bob Dole, a CNN/USA Today/Gallup poll said on Wednesday.

Pollsters found that 52 percent of 600 adults surveyed disagreed with the Commission on Presidential Debates recommendation to exclude Perot, 37 percent said he should be kept out and 11 percent had no opinion.
The survey was taken after the commission made its recommendation and had a margin of error of plus or minus 4 percentage points.
The Perot camp expressed outrage at the decision and said it would file a lawsuit to try to be included in the debates.

The commission, headed by Paul Kirk and Frank Fahrenkopf, former chairmen of the Democratic and Republican parties respectively, said Perot did not meet its chief criterion of having a "realistic" chance of winning on Nov. 5.
People polled agreed, with 87 percent saying Perot did not have a realistic chance to win and 9 percent saying he did. Of those surveyed 86 percent said they were not Perot supporters.
Clinton said he wanted Perot included while Dole, trailing the race for the White House, wanted a series of one-on-one encounters with Clinton.

The commission has proposed three presidential debates and one vice presidential debate, starting with a presidential debate on Sept. 25 in St. Louis, but the Clinton camp has rejected that date since Clinton is due to address the United Nations the day before and wants more time to prepare.
